title: A new idempotency key is made on every click, and the selection survives an unconfirmed refund, so a retry can refund twice
evidence: app.js:128 calls newIdempotencyKey() inside each refundSelected() call. The catch at app.js:131-133 leaves state.selected and state.orders untouched and the finally at 134-137 re-enables the button (renderRefundButton: disabled only when refunding, loading or n === 0). api.js:32 and README.md:9 say the key makes a repeated request safe, but the client never reuses a key, so the server cannot recognise a second click as a repeat.
failing_case: Select order 42 and click Refund, then confirm. The server issues the refund but the response is lost (connection drops, or a 502 from the proxy after the upstream call succeeded). The page shows 'The refund was not confirmed...'. The table still shows order 42 as paid and still checked, and the button is enabled. The user clicks Refund again (the message tells them to check before retrying, but nothing stops them). The second POST carries a different Idempotency-Key, so the server treats it as a new refund and the customer is refunded twice.
remediation: Keep the key with the pending attempt (same ids, same key) until the server confirms or the user changes the selection, and send that key on a retry. Also clear or lock the selection after an unconfirmed failure until a reload shows the real statuses.

title: normaliseOrder accepts a missing total as $0.00, although its own comment says such records are dropped
evidence: Number(null) is 0, Number('') is 0, Number([]) is 0, Number(false) is 0, and all are finite, so the guard at domain.js:12 (!Number.isFinite(total)) does not reject them. The comment at domain.js:7 and the 'skipped' notice in app.js:103 promise that records with no numeric total are dropped. Traced; not executed (shell unavailable).
failing_case: The API returns {"id":7,"customer":{"name":"Ann"},"status":"paid","total":null}. The row renders as $0.00, counts in the Orders stat, drags the average down, and the refund confirm shows a total that omits that order. No 'could not be shown' notice appears.
remediation: Accept only typeof raw.total === 'number' or a non-empty numeric string, then check Number.isFinite; add tests for null, '', [] and booleans.

quote: setMessage(`Orders could not be loaded. ${err.message}`, true);
title: A failed reload leaves the previous orders on screen, selectable and refundable
evidence: The catch (app.js:105-108) only sets a message. state.orders, state.selected and the table are not cleared or marked stale; renderRefundButton() in the finally (app.js:110) re-enables the refund button because state.selected is still non-empty and loading is false. After a successful refund, refundSelected() runs 'await load()' (app.js:130); if that load fails, the table still lists the just-refunded orders as paid and checked.
failing_case: Refund order 42 (success, toast 'Refunded 1 order.'), then the follow-up GET /orders fails with a 500. The page shows the error message, but the table still shows order 42 as paid with its box ticked and 'Refund 1 order' enabled. A second click refunds it again. The same stale table appears when a search for 'bob' fails: the rows for the previous query stay under the new search text.
remediation: On load failure clear state.orders and state.selected (or grey the table with a 'showing old results' notice and disable refunds) and offer a Retry button next to the message.

quote: const discounted = order.customer.tier === "gold" ? applyBp(cents, 10000 - GOLD_DISCOUNT_BP) : cents;
title: Revenue applies a gold discount and sales tax on top of order.total, while refunds use order.total as is; the two disagree for the same order
evidence: orderRevenueCents (domain.js:25-30) turns total into total x 0.9 (gold) x 1.0825. refundSelected sums raw o.total (app.js:122) for the confirm. Nothing in the payload says the API's total is a pre-discount, pre-tax subtotal.
failing_case: A gold customer's paid order has total 100.00. The Revenue card counts it as $97.43 (100 x 0.9 x 1.0825) and a standard-tier one as $108.25. The refund confirm for the same orders says $100.00. One of the two figures is wrong for any order; if total is already what the customer paid, revenue is overstated by 8.25% for standard and understated by 2.6% for gold.

requirement.why: No document says whether the API total is net or gross of tax and discount.

remediation: Settle in writing what the API total means, then have one pure function in domain.js produce the amount used by both the stats and the refund confirm, with a test for gold and standard orders.

title: Any order can be selected and sent for refund, whatever its status; no eligibility rule exists on the client
evidence: renderRow (app.js:34-60) gives every row an enabled checkbox. selectedOrders() (app.js:75-77) does not look at order.status. refundSelected() (app.js:119-123) then asks the user to confirm a total that includes refunded, pending and 'unknown' orders. The README's server list (README.md:6-10) covers who may refund, not whether an order is refundable, and domain.js holds no refund rule.
failing_case: Set Status to refunded, tick three rows, click 'Refund 3 orders'. The confirm reads 'Refund 3 orders totalling $X. This sends money back to the customers.' and a POST is sent for orders that were already refunded. If the server does not reject them, money goes out twice. If it does, the user still sees a confirm and a failure for an action the UI should not offer.
remediation: Add a pure canRefund(order) in domain.js (paid only), disable the checkbox for other statuses, and filter selectedOrders() through it. Give it a test.

title: Disabling a control while it has keyboard focus drops focus to the page start (refund button and pager)
evidence: The refund button is disabled when refunding starts (app.js:126 calls renderRefundButton) and while loading; Next is disabled on the last page (app.js:72) and Previous on the first (app.js:71). Browsers move focus off a disabled element. Inferred from browser behaviour; not driven (shell unavailable).
failing_case: A keyboard user tabs to Next and presses Enter until the last page: the button becomes disabled, focus falls to the body, and the next Tab starts from the top of the page. The same happens to the refund button after Enter: after the refund finishes focus is not restored.
remediation: Use aria-disabled with a guard in the handlers, or move focus to a sensible neighbour (Previous, the table, the status message) before disabling.

title: 'Average per order' divides paid revenue by every order, including refunded and pending
evidence: orderRevenueCents returns 0 for non-paid orders (domain.js:26), but the divisor is orders.length (domain.js:35). The same number feeds the 'Orders' card.
failing_case: One paid order of $100 and nine pending ones: the card shows Average per order $10.83 (approx; 108.25 / 10), although the only completed order is worth $108.25. Filtering by status=pending shows Revenue $0.00 and Average $0.00 instead of a dash.

requirement.why: The label implies revenue per order that produced revenue; no spec defines the divisor.

remediation: Divide by the count of orders that contributed revenue (paid), return null when that is zero, and label the Orders card to match.

title: The page heading is 24 px left of the content below it at wide widths
evidence: At 1360 px: .top has 24 px side padding, so h1 (max-width 1100, margin auto) starts at 24 + (1312-1100)/2 = 130 px. main is box-sizing border-box with max-width 1100, so its box starts at 130 px and its content (24 px padding) at 154 px (styles.css:24). Computed from the CSS; not rendered.
failing_case: On a 1360 px window, 'Orders' sits at x=130 while the stat cards, search field and table start at x=154.
remediation: Give .top h1 the same 24 px inline padding as main, or put the header content inside the same 1100 px wrapper as main.
